entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The present application, under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Section 528 of the BNSS), has been preferred seeking quashment of the order 14.09.2012 passed by Additional Sessions Judge, Chachoda, District Guna in Criminal Revision No.203 of 2011 whereby the order dated 09.08.2011 passed by Judicial Magistrate First Class, Chachoda in Case No.50 of 2006 was upheld.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge, Chachoda, District Guna
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Short facts of the case are that the complainant/petitioner was employed as a midwife at the Ayurvedic Dispensary, Sanai, from 1992 to 1999, while the respondent, Dr. Raghuvanshi, was posted as an Ayurvedic Medical Officer from 1983 to 1999.

During this period, the respondent allegedly manipulated official records, altered the sanctioned leaves of employees, and made unauthorized changes in the attendance register and casual leave register.

In this process, the petitioner/complainant claims that the respondent deliberately exploited her and tampered with her registers and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20861 2 MCRC-8157-2012 leave records.
The petitioner/complainant became aware of this in 2002, when she noticed discrepancies in her attendance at the Ayurvedic Dispensary, Sanai.
Upon obtaining certified copies of the attendance register, she realized the actual situation.
During this period, the respodent allegedly sent a forged document on 02.11.1996.

Subsequently, the then In-charge of the Ayurvedic Dispensary, Ratiram Bhaskar, filed a complaint on 21.11.2002, based on which instructions for punitive action against the respondent were issued, but no action was taken.
The petitioner/complainant also filed complaint/s on 02.11.2002, but again no action was taken thereon.

Therefore, a complaint was filed against the respondent under Sections 420, 467, 468, and 120B of Smt.Laxmi Bai vs Dr.Swarn Singh on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29117308/
1 the Indian Penal Code (IPC).

entities.text: Smt.Laxmi Bai vs Dr.Swarn Singh on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Based on the said complaint, the Judicial Magistrate First Class,
Chachoda took cognizance under Sections 468, 420, and 120-B of the IPC, relying on the statements of the petitioner/complainant Laxmibai and her witnesses.

Subsequently, after the respondent was present and the preliminary evidence was recorded, the respondent filed an application under Section 239 of the Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC), based on which an order dated 09.08.2011 was passed releasing the accused.

Being dissatisfied with the aforesaid order, the petitioner has filed Criminal Revision No.203 of 2011 before the Additional Sessions Judge, Chachoda, District Guna which was dismissed vide order dated 09.08.2011.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge, Chachoda, District Guna
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Hence, the present petition.

After hearing counsel for the petitioner and perusing the record, this Court finds that the respondent had sought clarification from the complainant/petitioner, Lakshmibai (PW-1), regarding certain alleged NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20861 3 MCRC-8157-2012 unethical relations.

This fact is further corroborated by the statement of Jayram Shakya (PW-2), which establishes that the respondent's conduct in this regard was not malicious or fraudulent but related to seeking clarity on personal or professional matters.
Furthermore, an FIR was filed by the petitioner/Lakshmibai against the respondent, which led to the initiation of a criminal case.
In the said case, the respondent was acquitted, indicating that the allegations against him were not substantiated to the satisfaction of the competent court.
This acquittal demonstrates that there was no prima facie evidence to suggest criminal culpability on the part of the respondnet.

The evidence and documents presented, including the statements of witnesses and official records,
do not prima facie indicate that the respondent attempted to cheat, forge, or tamper with documents with intention of causing harm to the petitioner/Lakshmibai (PW-1).
The allegations appear to be unsubstantiated when viewed in the light of the totality of the evidence.
The Judicial Magistrate First Class, after a detailed consideration of the facts, statements of witnesses, and the documentary evidence, passed the order releasing the respondent.
The order reflects a careful assessment of the merits of the complaint and is free from any apparent error of law or fact that would justify interference by this Court.
The scope of interference under Section 482 CrPC is well-settled.

In R.P. Kapur v. State of Punjab reported in AIR 1960 SC 866 and State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal reported in 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335,
the Apex Court laid down that inherent powers should be exercised sparingly, and only when the allegations do not disclose any offence or where continuation of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:20861 4 MCRC-8157-2012 proceedings would amount to abuse of the process of law.

entities.text: R.P. Kapur v. State of Punjab reported in AIR 1960 SC 866
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal reported in 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, in Amit Kapoor v. Ramesh Chander reported in (2012) 9 SCC 460 and State of Tamil Nadu v. N. Suresh Rajan reported in (2014) 11 SCC 709, it has been held that at the stage of framing of charge or discharge, the court is only to see whether a prima facie case is made out, and not to enter into a meticulous appreciation of evidence.

entities.text: Amit Kapoor v. Ramesh Chander reported in (2012) 9 SCC 460
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: State of Tamil Nadu v. N. Suresh Rajan reported in (2014) 11 SCC 709
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Likewise, in Madhavrao Jiwajirao Scindia v.
Sambhajirao Chandrojirao Angre reported in (1988) 1 SCC 692, it was held that where the chances of conviction are bleak and the proceedings would only result in abuse of process, interference may be justified.

entities.text:
Madhavrao Jiwajirao Scindia v.
Sambhajirao Chandrojirao Angre reported in (1988) 1 SCC 692
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Smt.Laxmi Bai vs Dr.Swarn Singh on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29117308/

2 Applying the aforesaid principles, this Court is of the opinion that the present case does not fall within the limited categories warranting the exercise of inherent jurisdiction under Section 482 CrPC.
The discharge of the respondent by the Judicial Magistrate, as affirmed by the revisional Court, is based on a proper appraisal of the evidence and does not call for interference.
In view of the foregoing discussion and the binding precedents of the Apex Court, the petition filed under Section 482 CrPC stands dismissed.
No further directions are called for.

(MILIND RAMESH PHADKE) JUDGE pwn*
